en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Thirteenth Chapter
The Discussion on Whether Craving for Existence is Indeterminate.
Is craving for existence indeterminate? Yes.
Is it the case that resultant indeterminate, functional indeterminate, matter, Nibbāna, the eye-base …pe… and the tangible-object-base [are all indeterminate]?
One should not say so …pe….
Is craving for existence (dhammataṇhā) indeterminate? Yes.
Is craving for form (rūpataṇhā) indeterminate?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is craving for phenomena (dhammataṇhā) indeterminate (abyākata)? Yes.
Craving for sounds … craving for odors … craving for tastes … [and so forth] … craving for tangibles … craving for mental phenomena.
Is craving for tangibles indeterminate?
You should not say so… [as before] … Is craving for forms unwholesome?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is craving for phenomena unwholesome?
You should not say so …pe…
Is craving for tastes …pe… craving for tangibles unwholesome? Yes.
Is craving for mental phenomena unwholesome?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Is craving for mental phenomena indeterminate?
“Yes.
“But has craving not been called unwholesome by the Blessed One?
“Yes.”
If craving has been declared unwholesome by the Blessed One, then indeed it should not be said that "craving for phenomena (dhammataṇhā) is indeterminate.
Is craving for phenomena indeterminate?
“Yes.
“But has it not been said by the Blessed One that greed is unwholesome, and that greed is craving for phenomena?
“Yes.”
If greed has been called unwholesome by the Blessed One, and craving for existence is greed, then surely it should not be said that "craving for existence is indeterminate.
Is craving for existence, which is greed, indeterminate?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then craving for form is greed and is indeterminate?
You should not speak thus …pe…
Is craving for existence (dhammataṇhā), which is greed, indeterminate?
Yes. Is craving for sound … [and so on] … indeterminate? Yes.
Is craving for tangibles (phoṭṭhabba-taṇhā) greed that is indeterminate (abyākata)?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Is craving for forms (rūpa-taṇhā) unwholesome greed (akusala-lobha)?
“Yes.
“Is craving for phenomena (dhammataṇhā) greed and unwholesome?
“One should not say so” … [and so on] …
Is craving for tastes … pe … craving for tangibles unwholesome greed? Yes.
Is craving for existence (dhammataṇhā) unwholesome greed?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is craving for existence indeterminate (abyākata)?
“Yes, [it is so].
“Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
‘That craving which leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and lust, finding delight here and there; that is to say:’?”
“Craving for sensual pleasure, craving for existence, and craving for non-existence.
Is this indeed a sutta?
Yes, it is.
Therefore, it should not be said that "craving for phenomena is indeterminate.
It should not be said [that way].
“Is craving for mental phenomena (dhammataṇhā) indeterminate (abyākatā)?
— “Yes.
— “But is it not indeed craving for mental phenomena?”
“Yes,” he replied.
“If that craving for phenomena is indeed craving for phenomena, then, indeed, it must be said:
‘Craving for phenomena is indeterminate.’”
The discussion on whether craving for existence is indeterminate is finished.
